direction: Perform dual-guided contact-graph surgery rather than random shaking: solve the final trust-region LP at the record, extract its dual variables or marginals for the active pairs, and identify the most stressed contacts and points, then run a constrained reoptimization in which 20–40 selected active pairs are forced to have cosine at most $\text{current max}-\delta$ for $\delta\in[5\times10^{-4},2\times10^{-3}]$, temporarily accepting an increase in other pairs before removing the forcing terms and LP-polishing. Repeat with different stressed clusters—highest-dual edges, high-degree points, and spatially localized patches—and keep candidates whose contact graph at a $10^{-5}$ threshold differs substantially, since a genuinely new topology is more promising than another nearly identical local optimum.

direction: Follow rigidity-nullspace directions to force a controlled contact exchange rather than using random kicks. idea: Build 1+6x27 two-plane cyclic symmetric codes and break symmetry by perturbation plus descent and LP polish.
direction: Search for a genuinely different symmetric seed using a two-plane cyclic orbit construction, then break the symmetry. Exploit $163=1+6\cdot27$: fix one pole and parameterize six representative unit vectors, generating each representative's orbit under simultaneous rotations through multiples of $2\pi/27$ in the $x_1x_2$ plane and multiples of $2\pi k/27$, for several integer twists $k$, in the orthogonal $x_3x_4$ plane. Optimize only the representatives with deterministic multi-start L-BFGS on an increasingly sharp soft-max objective, expand the best few symmetric configurations to all 163 points, randomly perturb them at several amplitudes, and release every point to short smooth descent plus LP polishing. Also try nearby orbit decompositions if an orbit degenerates, compare all candidates against the incumbent, and strictly return the best fully polished array within the time limit; even if exact symmetry is not optimal, its representatives may enter a basin inaccessible from the record.

Run several short deletion/addition cycles with different removed and inserted points, keeping an archive and returning the best verified 163-point result; moving through neighbouring cardinalities can reorganize contacts globally while avoiding dependence on a single random perturbation of the jammed record.

direction: Use frozen-background spherical-cap repacking to change the topology locally without destroying the globally good packing. Repeatedly select a cap centre from the rattler, a degree-8/9 hub, a low-degree point, or a random incumbent point; free the 10–14 points nearest that centre while freezing the other 149–153 points. Reinitialize the free points at diverse void candidates inside or near the cap, then optimize only those points against both frozen points and each other using annealed log-sum-exp/L-BFGS for a few hundred inexpensive iterations, followed by a global LP polish capped at about 3 seconds. Accept a repacking only after evaluating the complete $163\times4$ configuration, save improvements immediately, and rotate among cap sizes and centres under a hard internal deadline near 150 seconds; this targets the rattler and overloaded neighbourhoods while avoiding the repeated whole-configuration basin hops that previously timed out.

idea: Frozen-core weak-point deletion with large void sampling, soft-max void refinement, greedy mutual reinsertion and mobile-only annealed descent plus single short LP check.
direction: Do frozen-core rattler and low-degree deletion--reinsertion surgery: identify the rattler and all points with contact degree $\le4$, then try deleting sets of size $1,2,4,$ and $6$ drawn from these weak points while freezing the remaining high-degree core; for each deleted set, generate $50{,}000$ random unit quaternions, score them by maximum cosine to the retained core, take the best $200$ void candidates, locally refine them with a few log-sum-exp L-BFGS steps, and greedily reinsert points that are also mutually compatible. Only the reinserted points plus core points within slack $10^{-3}$ of them are then reoptimized with annealed smooth-max descent, the core staying fixed, followed by at most one short LP polish; accept a surgery only if the full $163$-point maximum cosine improves by at least $10^{-9}$, otherwise discard it, with a hard internal deadline near $150$ seconds and the incumbent returned on failure.

idea: Diversity-preserving memetic search with ICP-Kabsch plus Hungarian recombination of smooth-polished Hopf, random and perturbed incumbents, keeping LP only for the final polish.
direction: Run a diversity-preserving memetic population with cheap screening and recombination, reserving LP for the end: create $12$--$16$ starting codes from the incumbent perturbed at scales $0.01,0.03,0.1$, Hopf-layer codes, and random codes, polish each only with fast annealed smooth-max descent for a few seconds, and cluster them by contact-graph similarity after $SO(4)$ Kabsch alignment. For promising parent pairs, align them rotationally, match points with the Hungarian algorithm on cosine distance, form children by taking a principal-coordinate half or a connected contact-graph patch from one parent and the matched complement from the other, repair near-duplicate pairs by void reinsertion, and smooth-polish the children while selecting survivors by both score and contact-graph Hamming diversity. Only the best child and the incumbent receive LP polishing in the final $25$ seconds, all stages are deadline-aware, and the best feasible code encountered is always returned, avoiding the repeated expensive LP timeouts of earlier basin-hopping attempts.

idea: Layered Hopf-Clifford torus search with analytic smooth-max gradients over latitudes, phases and twists, then full-sphere descent and LP polish.
direction: Search de novo in a Hopf--Clifford torus layered ansatz instead of starting from the record: write points as $(\sin\chi_k\cos\theta,\sin\chi_k\sin\theta,\cos\chi_k\cos\phi,\cos\chi_k\sin\phi)$ on $M$ Clifford tori with layer latitudes $\chi_k$, counts $n_k$ summing to $163$, equispaced $(\theta,\phi)$ grids, layer phase offsets, and a twist parameter per layer. Randomly generate count allocations for $M=5$--$11$ layers, optimize only the resulting few dozen parameters $\{\chi_k,\text{phases},\text{twists}\}$ by smooth-max L-BFGS with temperatures $10^{-2}\to10^{-4}$, screen many allocations cheaply, then release the best two or three ansatz codes to full $163$-point smooth descent and a single final LP polish.
